A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DiMo-GUI research work, with readable text, algorithms, figures, tables, and references supporting a complete comparison. Neither contains an appendix; v2's final page is blank.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiMo-GUI benchmark evaluations in Tables 1–2 and zooming and modality ablations in Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and qualitative grounding examples in Section 4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 3 retain separate text/icon grounding, iterative cropping, the same stopping criterion, and candidate selection. Renaming DiMo-GUICondition to StopCondition does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ScreenSpot, labeled ScreenSpot-v2 in Table 2, and ScreenSpot-Pro. The mobile, desktop, web, and professional application coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparator membership, and Section 4.4 retains the same ablation comparisons. The newly cited Tao and Ge works are discussed only as related work, not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported datasets, sample counts, model configurations, accuracy comparisons, and zooming experiments are unchanged. Both retain half-size cropping, the one-sixth-diagonal stopping threshold, and the seven-iteration cap.

E4.justification: Both retain the zoom-count sweep in Table 3, dynamic-grounding and modality-decoupling ablations in Table 4, and the text-versus-icon case study in Figure 6. No additional robustness or supplementary analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both report point accuracies without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical entries and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, OS-Atlas-7B remains at 18.9 versus 49.7 with DiMo-GUI in Table 1, and 82.5 versus 85.7 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The coordinate notation and stopping-rule reasoning are retained, with no added or revised formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs. The stopping-predicate rename is purely terminological.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free, plug-and-play grounding through modality separation and dynamic zooming, including improved performance with minimal computational overhead.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 retain the explanations concerning resolution, lost context, and textual bias. Section 6 retains the limitation that early errors can become irrecoverable without backtracking and the same proposed future remedy.

D1.justification: The Figure 3 prompts, cropping and stopping details, model descriptions, and project homepage remain unchanged. v2 supplies no additional implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds brief discussions and references for Tao et al. (2025) on GUI localization errors and Ge et al. (2025) on Multi-Region Fusion Decoding. These modestly expand related-work coverage without redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 7, Acknowledgments, removes the first-author internship footnote, and corrects some malformed stopping terminology in Algorithm 1 and Section 3.1. Most prose and the existing section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The same six figures and four tables retain their content and designs. Minor page and column reflow changes their relationship to surrounding prose, and the added acknowledgments shift the references from page 8 to page 9.

improvement.justification: Replacing malformed stopping wording with StopCondition and stopped in Algorithm 1 and Section 3.1 modestly improves clarity. The two added related-work discussions and funding acknowledgments improve context and disclosure. These are limited gains: the scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and some wording errors persist.
